title: Lake Natron: Flamingos, Ol Doinyo Lengai and Desert Heat
excerpt: Lake Natron is hot, remote and spectacular: a red soda lake, the active volcano Ol Doinyo Lengai and the breeding ground of lesser flamingos.
body:
Lake Natron lies in the far north of Tanzania, near the Kenyan border, at the bottom of the Rift Valley. It is one of the most otherworldly landscapes in the country.

## The lake

Natron is an alkaline soda lake. Microorganisms can colour the shallow water red or pink. The water is caustic and not suitable for swimming.

## Flamingos

Lake Natron is the most important breeding site for lesser flamingos in East Africa. The breeding grounds themselves are hard to reach, but flamingos feed in the shallows along the shore. See [where to see flamingos](/blog/flamingos-tanzania/).

## Ol Doinyo Lengai

The "Mountain of God" for the Maasai is an active volcano. It is unusual because its lava is natrocarbonatite, which can appear black and turn white as it cools. Experienced hikers climb it at night; it is steep and demanding.

## Other activities

- A walk to waterfalls in a gorge near Ngare Sero, with pools to swim in.
- Walks along the lake shore with a Maasai guide.
- Searching for footprints at Engare Sero, a site with fossil human footprints.

## Practical

It is hot during the day. Roads are rough, and the drive from Mto wa Mbu or the Serengeti takes several hours. Accommodation is simple to comfortable tented camps.

Read our [Lake Natron page](/national-parks/lake-natron/) or [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
